questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following brainstem nuclei is not derived from the alar plate?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nucleus is not derived from the alar plate; it is a motor nucleus derived from the basal plate. In the developing neural tube, the basal plate forms motor nuclei and the alar plate forms sensory nuclei. The rhombic lip gives rise to the cerebellum and its nuclei.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 72-year-old patient who suffered a stroke is unable to swallow food. On examination, the gag reflex is absent. The motor nucleus of the vagus nerve involved here emerges from ______ of the brainstem.
questions.explanation: Fibers from nucleus ambiguus emerge through the posterolateral sulcus of the brainstem. Nucleus ambiguus contains motor components associated with cranial nerves IX, X and XI. The source also summarizes vagal components: dorsal vagal nucleus for parasympathetic output, nucleus ambiguus for pharynx/larynx/palate, nucleus tractus solitarius for viscero-sensory input, and spinal trigeminal nucleus for somatic sensory input from outer ear/dura.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 69-year-old male presented with diplopia. Investigations revealed an aneurysm of the right anterior inferior cerebellar artery that is directly impinging on the nerve arising at the pontomedullary junction. Which of the following extraocular muscles is likely to be paralyzed?
questions.explanation: The lateral rectus is most likely paralyzed because it is supplied by cranial nerve VI, which emerges at the pontomedullary junction. CN VI, VII and VIII arise at this junction. Superior oblique is supplied by IV; most other extraocular muscles by III.

Cranial nerves VI, VII, and VIII arise at the PMJ.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the nerve involved in the palsy shown below is false?

options.text: It divides into upper and lower divisions in its anterior part in the cavernous sinus.
Its divisions enter the orbit through the middle part of the superior orbital fissure.
It lies between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries in the interpeduncular fossa.
The nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion.
questions.explanation: The image shows oculomotor palsy. The false statement is that the nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion; these fibers travel with the nerve to inferior oblique. The oculomotor nerve passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, runs in the lateral wall of cavernous sinus, divides into superior and inferior divisions and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure/common tendinous ring.
